event.title: Jazz It Up with Sarto
event.description:
“Jazz It Up” with dinner, drinks and live music at the Sarto bar or in the dining room, as local trios perform hot Jazz from 6:30-8:30pm weekly on Saturdays.

Heading to a show downtown? Be sure to stop by Sarto after the show and enjoy music, dessert or bar snacks and a late-night libation.

Out with a group? Perfect! Plan ahead and make online reservations for table service for you and your friends, so everyone has a seat during Jazz it up with Sarto!

event.title: Brunch with Sarto
event.description:
Enjoy a full brunch menu packed with playful, elevated dishes. Offering appetizers like our “Italian Pop-Tart” (Caprese-style in puff pastry), Italian Poutine loaded with short rib and fontina cheese sauce, and the crowd-favorite Avocado Toast on toasted focaccia.

For entrées, the culinary team at Sarto has created modern Italian brunch offerings such as Eggs in Purgatory (poached eggs in fra diavolo sauce with grated gran padano and aleppo pepper, served with focaccia), the Nutella Crespella with strawberries and vanilla soil, and savory stars like the Steak Hash.

Pair it all with our specialty brunch cocktail menu, featuring Bottomless Mimosas, Bottomless Bellinis, and more!

Celebrate Sunday Funday with Brunch at Sarto, for a culinary brunch experience unlike any other in Providence!

Join Charleston Jazz for What a Wonderful World, an extraordinary celebration of jazz performance and education, at our annual fundraising gala on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

Inspired by Louis Armstrong’s lifelong commitment to jazz education and his belief that every musician has something worth sharing, What a Wonderful World will celebrate that spirit while investing in the future of jazz.

The evening features acclaimed trumpeter Bruce Harris who will take the stage alongside Charleston Jazz Orchestra musicians and talented students from the Charleston Jazz Academy for a one-of-a-kind performance. Bruce Harris is a gifted musician and educator with a deep respect for tradition while fearlessly exploring new musical ideas. What a Wonderful World: Featuring Bruce Harris

Louis Armstrong is considered one of the most important, if not the most important figure in the history of Jazz. His energetic and rhythmic playing has been a major influence on soloists of every genre of American popular music. Louis’ soaring trumpet and gravelly voice were made world famous with such favorites as Hello Dolly, Mack the Knife, Cheek to Cheek, and What a Wonderful World. 

Trumpet phenom Bruce Harris is an internationally renowned musician and educator and is Artistic Director of Programs at the Louis Armstrong House Museum in New York City. Throughout his career, Bruce has collaborated with many artists, to include Wynton Marsalis, Tony Bennett, Dave Brubeck and Samara Joy. On this special evening, Bruce joins the Charleston Jazz Orchestra for a Celebration of ‘Satchmo’ and the amazing music he created for the world to enjoy!

Concert Length: 90 min (no intermission)

This performance is made possible in part by MUSC

[/vc_column_text][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image image=”22097″ img_size=”full” alignment=”center” css=””][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1756145175171{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]About Bruce Harris

Bruce Harris, a Bronx-born trumpeter, is an acclaimed musician who blends tradition with innovation in New York City’s vibrant jazz scene. Influenced by the sounds of both Hip-hop and Be-bop, he began playing trumpet at age 12, drawing inspiration from legends like Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie, and Prince. His early talent led him to perform with Wynton Marsalis through the “Essentially Ellington” competition, later studying under Jon Faddis at SUNY Purchase, where he earned both a Bachelor’s and Master’s in Jazz Performance. Harris has since built a celebrated career performing at iconic venues such as Smalls, Smoke Jazz Club, and Dizzy’s Club, as well as appearing on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon. He has shared the stage with world-renowned artists, including Tony Bennett, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra. As a recording artist, he has released albums such as Beginnings, Soundview, and The Lighting of the Lamp, with a Barry Harris tribute album forthcoming on Equitone Records. Today, Harris tours globally as a soloist and bandleader, and he is set to honor Louis Armstrong at the renowned Newport Jazz Festival.

 [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_empty_space][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style=”flat” shape=”square” active_section=”1″][vc_tta_section title=”The Experience” tab_id=”1687923810144-42574a89-d6c9″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1691007354390{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]Often hailed as one of the top things to do in Charleston, SC, attending a Charleston Jazz Orchestra concert is an unforgettable experience.  If you are new to the jazz genre and big band style, take a risk and surprise yourself.  Our director Robert Lewis will guide you through the nuances and significance of each piece, sharing stories behind the songs and composers.  Many arrangements have been specially created by our own orchestra members and can’t be heard anywhere else in the world.  You can get a taste of past performances on our YouTube channel here.

When you step through the doors of the Charleston Music Hall you are stepping back in time into a circa 1849 train station, historically known as the Tower Depot.  You will hear the iconic sounds of jazz wafting through the lobby, reminiscent of the city’s rich jazz history.  Stop by one of the lobby bars on the lower or upper lever to purchase snacks, beer, wine or soft drinks to bring with you into the theatre. Our friendly ushers will greet you and assist you in finding your way to your seats – there’s not a bad seat in the house!

Our audience is diverse and you will see patrons of all ages and walks of life, including couples, singles, students, families, and groups of friends – jazz has never met a stranger and all are welcome.  Many of our guests are tourists visiting Charleston, and some of our regular attendees have been coming to concerts since the beginning of the organization.  We hope that you will become one of our “regulars” as well by joining the Charleston Jazz family by becoming a Season Subscriber, Member, Sponsor, Donor, Student or Advertiser.  There is a place for YOU at Charleston Jazz.

event.excerpt: Louis Armstrong is considered one of the most important, if not the most important figure in the history of Jazz. His energetic and rhythmic playing has been a major influence on soloists of every genre of American popular music. Louis’ soaring trumpet and gravelly voice were made world famous with such favorites as Hello Dolly, Mack the Knife, Cheek to Cheek, and What a Wonderful World. Trumpet phenom Bruce Harris is an internationally renowned musician and educator and is Artistic Director of Programs at the Louis Armstrong House Museum in New York City. Throughout his career, Bruce has collaborated with many artists, to include Wynton Marsalis, Tony Bennett, Dave Brubeck and Samara Joy. On this special evening, Bruce joins the Charleston Jazz Orchestra for a Celebration of ‘Satchmo’ and the amazing music he created for the world to enjoy!

Embrace the festive spirit with the Charleston Jazz Orchestra’s highly anticipated annual extravaganza, Holiday Swing. Tommy Brown Jr. is a Lowcountry native and advocate for creative expression. He studied engineering at South Carolina State University and worked as an industrial engineer before deciding to pursue his musical career full-time. Tommy has been singing since the age of 9 and has shared the stage with many artists locally and internationally. As a lover of all music, he started his musical explorations in church singing gospel only to further expand his experiences across all genres.

 [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_empty_space][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style=”flat” shape=”square” active_section=”1″][vc_tta_section title=”The Experience” tab_id=”1687923810144-42574a89-d6c9″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1691007354390{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]Often hailed as one of the top things to do in Charleston, SC, attending a Charleston Jazz Orchestra concert is an unforgettable experience.  If you are new to the jazz genre and big band style, take a risk and surprise yourself.  Our director Robert Lewis will guide you through the nuances and significance of each piece, sharing stories behind the songs and composers.  Many arrangements have been specially created by our own orchestra members and can’t be heard anywhere else in the world.  You can get a taste of past performances on our YouTube channel here.

When you step through the doors of the Charleston Music Hall you are stepping back in time into a circa 1849 train station, historically known as the Tower Depot.  You will hear the iconic sounds of jazz wafting through the lobby, reminiscent of the city’s rich jazz history.  Stop by one of the lobby bars on the lower or upper lever to purchase snacks, beer, wine or soft drinks to bring with you into the theatre. Our friendly ushers will greet you and assist you in finding your way to your seats – there’s not a bad seat in the house!

Our audience is diverse and you will see patrons of all ages and walks of life, including couples, singles, students, families, and groups of friends – jazz has never met a stranger and all are welcome.  Many of our guests are tourists visiting Charleston, and some of our regular attendees have been coming to concerts since the beginning of the organization.  We hope that you will become one of our “regulars” as well by joining the Charleston Jazz family by becoming a Season Subscriber, Member, Sponsor, Donor, Student or Advertiser.  There is a place for YOU at Charleston Jazz.

width=”1/6″][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1786640594607{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]Getz & Jobim at 100: BeBop Meets Bossa Nova

Two legends. One evening. Celebrate the centennial birthdays of saxophone icon Stan Getz and Brazilian composer Antônio Carlos Jobim — two artists whose singular genius and historic collaboration transformed jazz forever. From the blazing swing of “Four Brothers” to the timeless elegance of “The Girl from Ipanema” and “Corcovado,” the Charleston Jazz Orchestra captures the warmth, improvisation, and irresistible rhythms that made Bossa Nova a global phenomenon. Featuring vocalist Heather Rice.

Concert Length: 90 min (no intermission)[/vc_column_text][vc_empty_space][vc_separator css=””][vc_empty_space][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image image=”23334″ img_size=”full” alignment=”center” css=””][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1785180530417{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]About Stan Getz:

Stan Getz (1927-1991) was an American jazz tenor saxophonist, known as one of the best musicians of jazz’s “cool school,” and noted for his mellow tone.

Getz began studying saxophone at 13 and debuted professionally at 15. His breakthrough came in 1947 as one of Woody Herman’s “Four Brothers,” who specialized in cool-toned modern jazz. In the 1950s, Getz led quartets and quintets.

After living in Europe from 1958 to 1961, Getz ushered in the bossa nova era in 1962 after teaming up with guitarist Charlie Byrd to record Jazz Samba, which included their hit recording of “Desafinado.” He collaborated with Brazilian musicians on the album Getz/Gilberto (1963), which became one of the best-selling jazz albums of all time and included the hit song “The Girl from Ipanema”.

Source: Brittanica.com [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_empty_space][vc_separator css=””][vc_empty_space][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1785180546612{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]About Carlos Jobim:

Antônio Carlos Jobim (1927–1994) was a Brazilian songwriter, composer, and arranger who transformed the Brazilian samba’s rhythms into an intimate music called bossa nova.

Also known as “Tom,” Jobim began playing piano at 14 and was inspired by Brazilian composer Heitor Villa-Lobos. Initially not wanting to pursue music, he became disenchanted with architecture and devoted himself to music. In 1958, Jobim collaborated with singer-guitarist João Gilberto, and their song “Chega de Saudade” (also known as “No More Blues”) became the first bossa nova single.

Jobim collaborated on many albums, such as Getz/Gilberto (1963) and Frank Sinatra & Antonio Carlos Jobim (1967). Some of his popular songs include “One-Note Samba,” “Desafinado,” “Meditação,” “Corcovado,” “The Girl from Ipanema,” “Wave,” and “Dindi”.

Source: Brittanica.com [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image image=”23333″ img_size=”full” alignment=”center” css=””][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_empty_space][vc_separator css=””][vc_empty_space][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_single_image image=”23297″ img_size=”full” alignment=”center” css=””][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/2″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1785180554455{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]About Heather Rice:

Heather Rice is a Charleston-based singer songwriter known for her powerful voice, intelligent songwriting, and dynamic concerts; most notably A Tribute to Joni Mitchell. She is an opener for Joan Osborne, Sheryl Crow, and Lady Antebellum. Rice co-wrote the song, “Like Make Believe” for Hootie and the Blowfish artist, Mark Bryan, and was a featured performer in the drama desk award-winning show, Toxic Audio.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_empty_space][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/2″][vc_empty_space height=”24px”][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_empty_space][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][vc_tta_accordion style=”flat” shape=”square” active_section=”1″][vc_tta_section title=”The Experience” tab_id=”1687923810144-42574a89-d6c9″][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1691007354390{margin-bottom: 0px !important;}”]Often hailed as one of the top things to do in Charleston, SC, attending a Charleston Jazz Orchestra concert is an unforgettable experience.  If you are new to the jazz genre and big band style, take a risk and surprise yourself.  Our director Robert Lewis will guide you through the nuances and significance of each piece, sharing stories behind the songs and composers.  Many arrangements have been specially created by our own orchestra members and can’t be heard anywhere else in the world.  You can get a taste of past performances on our YouTube channel here.

When you step through the doors of the Charleston Music Hall you are stepping back in time into a circa 1849 train station, historically known as the Tower Depot.  You will hear the iconic sounds of jazz wafting through the lobby, reminiscent of the city’s rich jazz history.  Stop by one of the lobby bars on the lower or upper lever to purchase snacks, beer, wine or soft drinks to bring with you into the theatre. Our friendly ushers will greet you and assist you in finding your way to your seats – there’s not a bad seat in the house!

Our audience is diverse and you will see patrons of all ages and walks of life, including couples, singles, students, families, and groups of friends – jazz has never met a stranger and all are welcome.  Many of our guests are tourists visiting Charleston, and some of our regular attendees have been coming to concerts since the beginning of the organization.  We hope that you will become one of our “regulars” as well by joining the Charleston Jazz family by becoming a Season Subscriber, Member, Sponsor, Donor, Student or Advertiser.  There is a place for YOU at Charleston Jazz.

 

I have been a season ticket holder since the inception of Charleston Jazz Orchestra for many wonderful reasons. The caliber of performances are spectacular. Their musical selections appeal to all musical tastes regardless of age. The Music Hall is the perfect venue for such a group of phenomenal artists.

Columbia, SC – September 14, 2026 – One Columbia Arts and Culture is opening its doors this Hispanic Heritage Month for “Puentes del Arte,” a free community Open House celebrating the richness of Hispanic culture through art, music, and food. The event takes place Thursday, October 1, from 6-8 PM at 801 Wildwood Avenue, Columbia, SC 29203.

“Puentes del Arte” means “Bridges of Art,” and that’s exactly the spirit One Columbia hopes to capture: connection, celebration, and community, all built around creativity. Guests can look forward to an evening full of color and rhythm, with live music from David Rodriguez and The Latin Hustle setting the tone for the night.

Attendees will also have the opportunity to view art through a collaboration with Palmetto Luna Arts, a local organization dedicated to promoting Latino arts and culture in the Midlands. And no celebration is complete without great food. Takosushi will be on-site serving up its signature flavors, adding one more layer of cultural connection to the evening.

“Last year, we hosted our first open house at the Keenan House, and it was a tremendous success. Our goal was simple: to create a welcoming space for community and connection while reintroducing people to One Columbia,” said Xavier Blake, Executive Director of One Columbia Arts and Culture. “As we began planning this year’s event, we asked ourselves how we could be even more intentional. Our board had the wonderful idea of celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month in partnership with Limitless Community Development and from that vision, Puentes del Arte was born. This year’s open house will serve as a special kickoff to Carnaval del Barrio, taking place Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Finlay Park. Carnaval del Barrio is another incredible event celebrating the Hispanic cultures, creativity, and community that enrich our city. We look forward to celebrating with you in October!”

Tanya Rodriguez-Hodges, Executive Director of Limitless Community Development, echoed that spirit of unity: “Celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month is about more than honoring culture; it is about opening our hearts to one another, learning from our neighbors, and creating a community where everyone feels welcome. We are grateful to partner with One Columbia Arts and Culture on Puentes del Arte and invite people from every background to experience the beauty, creativity, and traditions of Hispanic heritage. This meaningful evening will lead into Carnaval del Barrio, a free community celebration on Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Finlay Park. Together, these events remind us that when we share our stories and celebrate our cultures, we build stronger bridges and bring our communities closer together.”

Whether you’re an art enthusiast, a longtime supporter of multicultural events, or simply looking for a fun night out in Columbia, “Puentes del Arte” offers something for everyone. It’s a chance to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month in a way that feels personal, artistic, and deeply rooted in community.

The event is free and open to the public. RSVPs can be made through Eventbrite at eventbrite.com/e/open-house-puentes-del-arte-tickets-2001007493278, so guests can simply show up ready to enjoy the music, art, and food.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

Limitless Community Development is proud to announce the return of Carnaval del Barrio, one of the Midlands’ largest celebrations of Hispanic Heritage month, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at Finlay Park in downtown Columbia with free entry.

Limitless Community Development is honored to recognize Wells Fargo Bank as the Premier Sponsor of Carnaval del Barrio 2026. Their generous support will help make this year’s celebration possible and expand access to an inclusive cultural experience for families throughout South Carolina.

Drawing hundreds of attendees each year, Carnaval del Barrio is a family-friendly festival that celebrates the rich traditions, diversity, and contributions of the diverse Hispanic community through live entertainment, authentic cuisine, cultural performances, local artisans, community resources, and interactive activities for all ages.
Hosted by Limitless Community Development, the festival serves as more than a cultural celebration, it is an opportunity to bring communities together, support local businesses, and connect families with valuable community resources in an inclusive and welcoming environment.

“Carnaval del Barrio is more than a festival, it is a celebration of our community’s rich cultural heritage and an opportunity to bring people together through music, art, food, and shared experiences. Each year, we strive to create an inclusive event where every family feels welcomed, connected, and proud to celebrate the diversity that makes our community so special,” said Tanya Rodriguez-Hodges, Executive Director of Limitless Community Development.

Festival attendees can enjoy:
• Free Entry
• Live music by local artists DJ Angel, Los Del 9-54, David Rodriguez, and Latin Hustle
• Live musical performances by international artists MXKA and Bella Dose
• Cultural Dance performances
• A variety of food vendors
• Artisan and marketplace vendors
• Community resource organizations
• Family-friendly activities

As one of the premier cultural events held at Finlay Park, Carnaval del Barrio continues to strengthen community connections while celebrating the vibrant traditions and diversity of the community throughout South Carolina.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

event.description:
The Koger Center for the Arts has set the headliners for the first Levitt AMP Columbia Music Series, a series of free outdoor concerts sponsored in part by the Levitt Foundation. The concerts will take place on the Plaza Stage on the Koger Center’s front lawn from 5:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m., with the rain location being indoors in either the Black Box Theater or second floor lobby.

The Levitt AMP Columbia Music Series is dedicated to uplifting Columbia as a cultural hub and destination for accessible entertainment. The series is supported by a variety of community partners, including the Jasper Project, ONE Columbia, ColaJazz, South Carolina Philharmonic, University of South Carolina Student Life, Black Nerd Mafia, the South Carolina Commission for Community Advancement and Engagement, the Columbia Chamber, the Vista Guild and the City of Columbia.

Geared to towns and cities with populations under 250,000, Levitt AMP grantees reflect the three goals of the LevittAMP Music Series program: Amplify community pride and a city’s unique character; enrich lives through the power of free, live Music; and illustrate the importance of inclusive and vibrant public Places. From rural Alaska to Appalachian Main Streets and Midwestern locales, Levitt AMP is a catalytic opportunity for towns and cities across America to realize a shared mission—building community through music to create a healthy and thriving future for all. Columbia is the only Levitt AMP location in South Carolina.

Columbia residents are encouraged to follow along with the development of the series over the next three years by visiting www.KogerCenterForTheArts.com, and following @LevittAmpColumbia and @KogerCenterForTheArts on Instagram.

The beloved community event invites artists, art lovers, educators, students, and families out for a day of hands-on creativity as Columbia transforms into a vibrant, open-air gallery.

The festival offers free admission and provides participants of all skill levels the opportunity to create their own concrete masterpieces. Grounds will be sectioned into individual squares, giving every artist—seasoned pros and first-time doodlers alike—a dedicated canvas to showcase their talent and imagination.

This year Artlinc will be held at the Vista Greenway Trail Entrance (under the Elmwood Street overpass). The Vista Greenway Trail is the gateway to trail that connects Finlay Park to the Lincoln Tunnel that opening up in the entertainment district of the Vista.

 

” ArtLinc is a celebration to showcase our talented artists and bring our community together. Whether you consider yourself an artist or just want to pick up a piece of chalk and express yourself, everyone is invited to be part of the fun.”

 

Event Highlights & Details:

Interactive Chalking: Dedicated squares for artists, patrons, and kids to create custom chalk artwork.

Free Materials: Chalk will be provided free of charge on-site, though participants are welcome to bring their own supplies.

Family-Friendly & Free: Admission is 100% free for all attendees.

Whether you’re coming to paint the pavement, support local creators, or simply enjoy the colorful atmosphere, the 7th ArtLinc Chalk Arts Festival promises an inspiring afternoon for the entire community.

For more information, vendor details, or event updates, visit www.ArtlincSC.com.

About ArtLinc

ArtLinc is an annual festival dedicated to celebrating community, creativity, and local talent in Columbia, S.C. By providing an inclusive space for people of all ages and artistic backgrounds to make art together, ArtLinc aims to foster a deeper appreciation for visual arts and community connection.[/vc_column_text][image_with_animation image_url=”785587″ image_size=”full” max_width=”50%” max_width_mobile=”default” animation_type=”entrance” animation=”None” animation_movement_type=”transform_y” hover_animation=”none” alignment=”” border_radius=”none” box_shadow=”none” image_loading=”default”][/vc_column][/vc_row]

event.title: Women in Wine Dinner
event.description:
This event has been rescheduled to Wednesday, October 28th.

Women in Wine: An Evening in Secret Cocktail Garden

High above downtown Greenville’s Main Street, Juniper’s Secret Cocktail Garden sets the stage for an intimate evening celebrating the women behind some of the wine world’s most distinctive and celebrated bottles.

Get Tickets

Surrounded by lush greenery, warm candlelight, and the glow of downtown Greenville, guests will gather around the table for an evening dedicated to women-owned and women-made wineries, paired with a menu created to highlight the character and story behind each wine.

From crisp Sauvignon Blanc to rich Cabernet Sauvignon and bold Shiraz, each pour has been thoughtfully selected to showcase the craftsmanship and vision of women in the wine industry. The evening unfolds course by course, inviting guests to experience these wines alongside an elevated menu designed specifically for the occasion.

Guests will enjoy a thoughtfully curated four-course dinner followed by dessert, including:

First Course
Emmolo Sauvignon Blanc
PEI mussels, Thai green curry, kaffir lime, Fresno chilis, shrimp toast

Second Course
Flowers Chardonnay
Pumpkin agnolotti, stracciatella, brown butter, hazelnut, black truffle

Third Course
Charles Krug Cabernet Sauvignon
Gnocchi alla Romana, braised oyster mushrooms, Swiss chard, Parmigiano Reggiano

Fourth Course
Ferrari Siena Red Blend
Duck, duck, goose — duck two ways, foie gras, Brussels sprouts, sweet potato hash, pomegranate gastrique

Dessert
Mollydooker Shiraz
Dark chocolate genoise, blueberry mousse, pecan crumble, Shiraz sorbet

More than a dinner, Women in Wine is an opportunity to raise a glass to the women shaping the world of wine — from the vineyards and cellars to the bottle in your glass.

Seats are limited. Reserve your place for an unforgettable evening of exceptional food, remarkable wines, and a celebration of women in wine, all beneath the open sky in Juniper’s Secret Cocktail Garden.

Please notify Baileigh.Wilson@acmarriott.com of any dietary restrictions or accommodations needed at the time of booking.

event.title: SDSU Day
event.description:
Jackrabbit spirit takes over the Washington Pavilion and Main Avenue for a day of science, engineering and hands-on discovery! See SDSU innovation in action through student projects, demonstrations and interactive experiences featuring South Dakota State University students and faculty.

Friday, Oct. 2

10 a.m.-3 p.m. | Scheduled school group programming
5-8 p.m. | Free First Friday + public activities

Join Us for the Evening!

The public is invited to experience SDSU Day during Free First Friday from 5-8 p.m., with SDSU activities happening approximately 5-7:30 p.m.

Get an up-close look at SDSU Engineering’s NASA competition rovers, explore student projects and demonstrations and enjoy hands-on activities for kids and families.

Plus, at 6 p.m. in the Sweetman Planetarium, hear from Dr. Todd Letcher as he kicks off a new science and research speaker series highlighting SDSU research and innovation.

Museum admission is FREE from 5-8 p.m., so make a night of it and explore the Kirby Science Discovery Center and Visual Arts Center while you’re here.

event.title: Plays for Living: Public Performance
event.description:
An Evening with Plays for Living

Oct. 5, 2026 | 7 p.m.
Belbas Theater
Free admission

Celebrate 25 years of Plays for Living with a free public performance featuring three short, thought-provoking plays presented by young performers from Spotlight Theatre Company.

Plays for Living brings educational, conversation-starting theatre into schools and throughout the community. Each play explores an important social issue, helping audiences build awareness, consider new perspectives and begin meaningful conversations.

Featured Plays

What’s the Difference?

Recommended for fourth grade and older

This fast-paced performance inspired by the classic Alice in Wonderland story explores diversity, discrimination, bullying, stereotypes and cliques.

By William Baldwin Young
Directed by Abby Schwedhelm

Cast:

  • Hadley Hodak as Leonard
  • Lily Smith as Alice
  • Sophia Flores as Max
  • Sydney Carolan as Ms. Teal
  • Zoey Lemke as Bertrand

¿Cuál Es La Diferencia?

Recommended for fourth grade and older

Performed in Spanish, this fast-paced production inspired by the classic Alice in Wonderland story explores diversity, discrimination, bullying, stereotypes and cliques.

By William Baldwin Young
Translated into Spanish by Eileen Baumgarten
Directed by Rebekah Merriman

Cast:

  • Diem Anderson as Ms. Teal
  • Hailey Hernandez as Alice
  • Hanalei Barrett as Max
  • Macie Miles as Leonard
  • Mikayla Jundt as Bertrand

Devon’s Hurt

Recommended for second grade and older

This play helps young audiences explore hurt feelings and learn healthy ways to understand and cope with them.

By Laurie Brooks
Directed by Tatiana Chance

Cast:

  • Ellianna Dengler as Stephanie
  • Hailey Hernandez as Devon
  • Jessica Graeber as Hurt
  • Teddi Maxon as Sam

Plays for Living is supported by the Midco Foundation and the Sercl Family Fund through the Sioux Falls Area Community Foundation.

event.description:
Trampled by Turtles are from Duluth, Minnesota, where frontman Dave Simonett initially formed the group as a side project in 2003. At the time, Simonett had lost most of his music gear, thanks to a group of enterprising car thieves who’d ransacked his vehicle while he played a show with his previous band. Left with nothing more than an acoustic guitar, he began piecing together a new band, this time taking inspiration from bluegrass, folk, and other genres that didn’t rely on amplification.
Simonett hadn’t played any bluegrass music before, and he filled his lineup with other newcomers to the genre, including fiddler Ryan Young (who’d previously played drums in a speed metal act) and bassist Tim Saxhaug. Along with mandolinist Erik Berry and banjo player Dave Carroll, the group began carving out a fast, frenetic sound that owed as much to rock & roll as bluegrass.
There crossover appeal has landed them on the #1 spot of Billboard’s Bluegrass Charts on every record they’ve released while playing marquee festivals like Coachella, ACL Fest, and Lollapalooza. Countless tours with diverse artists ranging Shakey Graves, Zach Bryan, Wilco, Caamp, Mt Joy, Willie Nelson, Avett Brothers, Lord Huron and many more have followed solidifying a loyal fanbase. Their last full length album Alpenglow was produced by Wilco’s Jeff Tweedy. 2025 began with the band releasing a cover of Bon Iver’s “From Emma” with Caamp’s Taylor Meier (aka Sumbuck) on lead vocals. A few new collaborations are set to be announced in the coming weeks.

event.title: Could You Hug a Cactus? Presented by Spotlight Theatre Company
event.description:
Book by Jessica Penzias
Music and Lyrics by Denver Casado

What happens when a group of kids lets its imagination run wild?

Could You Hug a Cactus? is a playful musical revue bursting with poetry, music and creativity. One by one, young performers step into the spotlight to share imaginative creations about towering robots, homemade forts, hungry monsters and plenty of wonderfully unexpected ideas.

But when one nervous performer struggles to share a poem, the cast comes together to help him overcome his self-doubt and discover his own creative spark. Whimsical, funny and uplifting, this family-friendly production celebrates confidence, self-expression and the joy of creating something that is uniquely yours.

Single tickets go on sale Jan. 13.

event.title: MARK TWAIN TONIGHT!
event.description:
Emmy-Award® winning Actor and 2025 Theater Hall of Fame Inductee Richard Thomas brings to life “the nation’s one true comic genius” (The New York Times) in Mark Twain Tonight!, written and originally performed by Hal Holbrook. Join the millions who have cheered for the legendary one-man show, bursting with Twain’s “uproariously funny” and “pungently wise” (Time Magazine) humor.

Most recently seen on Broadway in Our Town, on tour as Atticus Finch in To Kill a Mockingbird, and on Netflix’s Ozark, Richard Thomas will return to Broadway in Spring 2026 in David Lindsay-Abaire’s The Balusters, directed by Kenny Leon. Beloved to generations as John-Boy Walton, Richard Thomas is the first and only actor authorized to perform Mark Twain Tonight! since the original.

event.title: Plays for Living: Public Performance
event.description:
An Evening with Plays for Living

March 30, 2027 | 7 p.m.
Belbas Theater
Free admission

Join us for a free public performance featuring three short, thought-provoking plays presented by young performers from Spotlight Theatre Company.

Now celebrating its 25th anniversary, Plays for Living uses theatre to explore important social issues and inspire meaningful conversations. These performances invite audiences to experience the program beyond its school and community tour.

Featured Plays

Survivors

Recommended for seventh grade and older

This play explores depression and suicide prevention while encouraging teenagers to recognize the importance of hope, support and seeking help.

By Leslie Glass
Directed by Jeff Larsen

Cast:

  • Aidan Wescott as Eric
  • Alexa Robbins as Mary
  • Bella Maxon as Tiffany
  • Kaiden Jundt as Jerry
  • Mikayla Jundt as Stephanie

Monster in the Mirror

Recommended for fourth grade and older

Blending humor and drama, this play follows middle schoolers navigating online bullying and body image while exploring the impact of online behavior.

By Katelynn Kenney
Directed by Dr. Jayna Gearhart Fitzsimmons

Cast:

  • Autumn Noteboom as Mirror Quinn/Fairy Dog Mother
  • Ellie Brown as Jo
  • Emelia DeJong as Mirror Jo/Todd the Frog
  • Madeleine Gedney as Narrator/Professors
  • Scarlett Sampson as Quinn

A New Norm

Recommended for third grade and older

Based on the book by Tom Roberts, this musical explores anxiety, depression, grief, anger, doubt, shame and fear while reminding audiences that hope and help are available.

By Luke Tatge, based on the book by Tom Roberts
Directed by Molly Wilson
Music directed by Beth Rygg

Cast:

  • Aidan Wescott as Norm
  • Allison Zuercher as Mom
  • Bella Maxon as Spark
  • Kaiden Jundt as Dad
  • Sawyer Winters as Darkness
  • Shay Boetel as Tornado

Plays for Living is supported by the Midco Foundation and the Sercl Family Fund through the Sioux Falls Area Community Foundation.
event.excerpt: Celebrate 25 years of Plays for Living with three thought-provoking plays presented by young Spotlight Theatre Company performers. Admission is free.

event.title: The Okee Dokee Brothers
event.description:
​​Childhood friends, Joe Mailander and Justin Lansing, have been exploring the outdoors together since they were kids growing up in Denver, Colorado. Whether making forts by the neighborhood creek or camping in the mountains, their friendship was built on imagination and adventure. Today, as the GRAMMY Award-winning Okee Dokee Brothers, they turn that spirit into Americana folk songs that celebrate friendship, nature and the joy of discovery.

Their music has been called “the Shel Silverstein of family music” for the way it reaches both kids and parents. With banjo, guitar and brotherly harmony at the heart of their sound, they create songs that make you want to dance in the kitchen and sing by the campfire. Blending humor and heart, their work reminds listeners that wisdom can be simple, and that the best adventures can begin right outside your door.

The duo’s playful yet thoughtful songwriting has earned praise from NPR’s All Things Considered and USA Today, along with five Parents’ Choice Awards and a GRAMMY® for Best Children’s Album. They’ve been featured on PBS KIDS and Netflix for their short family films.

On their newest album, Little Old You, The Okee Dokee Brothers are going back to basics with an acoustic backyard set from the heart. Banjo and guitar take the lead on these playful songs full of life and the mystery of the natural world. It’s a big bucket full of sticks, mud and cosmic wonder. Joe and Justin continue to remind us that we are both silly and wise, young and old and infinitely big in all our little ways.

The Okee Dokee Brothers’ songs have become soundtracks for family adventures and everyday moments alike, offering comfort, laughter and a gentle nudge toward the wild and unplugged natural world. Their approach is guided by a few steady truths: friendship matters, nature connects us, laughter opens doors and the smallest things (and people) often hold the biggest magic.

Taking place from November 30 to December 2, 2026, the event will be held at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center in Saudi Arabia.  The three-day exhibition brings together over 7,000 mobility professionals and more than 100 exhibitors, driving smart infrastructure and transport efficiency. The event is taking place against the backdrop of Saudi Arabia’s massive transport and logistics infrastructure investment program. It is co-located with both the Global Transport Expo and the Saudi Parking Expo to create a unified ecosystem for the industry.  The key areas of focus for this year’s expo will include: -Roads: Traffic management systems, artificial intelligence in monitoring, and safety equipment.
-Rail & Transport: Urban metro projects, public transit, autonomous vehicles, and electric vehicle (EV) infrastructure. -Parking: Smart parking technologies, on-street/off-street solutions, and access control.

event.title: Finding Home | Songs of Love & Justice Benefit Concert
event.description:
An Evening with Cheryl Slay Carr
Finding Home: Songs of Love and Justice
A Benefit Concert Supporting I Am Next 

Date: Friday, October 9, 2026
Doors Open: 6:15 PM
Concert: 7:00 PM
Location: National Museum of African American Music | 510 Broadway, Nashville, TN 37203

Join us for Finding Home: Songs of Love and Justice, a powerful evening of music, storytelling, and community led by acclaimed vocalist Cheryl Slay Carr and featured guest artist — MarQo “Q” Patton.

Finding Home explores the many meanings of “home”— from love and identity to resilience, faith, justice, and belonging. Each song becomes part of a larger musical journey, inviting audiences to reflect on the places, people, and experiences that shape who we are and where we find a sense of home.

Presented as a benefit performance supporting I Am Next, Finding Home is more than a concert—it is an evening rooted in the power of music to connect us, inspire us, and move us toward a more just and compassionate future.

Come find your way home.

About I Am Next:
I Am Next  supports youth aging out of foster care by empowering youth with the resources, relationships and much-needed time to find their footing and build lasting stability.

event.title: In The Pocket | A Celebration with Lee Garrett
event.description:
The National Museum of African American Music Presents
In The Pocket
A Celebration with Lee Garrett

Saturday, October 17, 2026 | 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM 
Amplify Lounge | National Museum of African American Music 

Join the National Museum of African American Music for a special edition of In The Pocket, celebrating the life, music, and legacy of Grammy-nominated songwriter, artist, and radio pioneer Lee Garrett.

Garrett’s career is woven into the fabric of American music. With songwriting credits including ‘Signed, Sealed, Delivered I’m Yours’ (co-written with Stevie Wonder), The Spinners’ ‘It’s a Shame’ and Jermaine Jackson’s ‘Let’s Get Serious,’ ‘Better Than Walking Out’ by Marlena Shaw and ‘Heart Be Still’ for Frankie Valli. He made history as the first blind Top 40 radio DJ, and this year marks the 50th anniversary of his original Heat for the Feets, featuring UK hit  ‘You’re My Everything’.

Moderated by Grammy Award-winning musician and producer Shannon Sanders, this intimate conversation will take audiences behind the songs and defining moments of Lee Garrett’s journey — where he’ll share stories from his career, reflect on his friendships and creative relationships, and explore the impact their generation of artists and songwriters have had on music and culture.

event.title: FIRST NOTE: For The Love of R&B
event.description:
Memphis’ emerging sound joins forces with Nashville’s, and NMAAM is capturing this unforgettable story on an unforgettable night.

The National Museum of African American Music and TappedIN 901 proudly present First Note: For the Love of R&B, a groundbreaking show created to magnify the musical connection between Memphis and Nashville, TN. Born from a simple but radical belief: emerging artists deserve more than a stage. They deserve a platform.

Beginning October 24, NMAAM will become the epicenter of something new—a conduit bridging the soulful sound of Memphis with the harmony of Music City. Artists who are just writing their first chapters will share space with fans who feel it, industry executives who need to hear it, and a community of museum visitors who will carry those sounds far beyond these walls.

Memphis and Nashville share a story, and NMAAM is the home where the next chapter begins.

event.title: Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission
event.description:
Opening Sept. 29, 2026

Get Tickets

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission invites guests to step into the story behind the 1985 discovery of the RMS Titanic and uncover the classified U.S. Navy mission that helped make it possible.

Visitors can follow the clues that led oceanographer Dr. Robert Ballard and his team to Titanic, learn how deep-sea technology was used to explore more than two miles beneath the North Atlantic, and discover how a secret mission to survey the wrecks of the USS Thresher and USS Scorpion ultimately helped solve one of history’s greatest mysteries.

Along the way, guests will explore the story of Titanic itself, from its launch in 1911 and tragic maiden voyage to the decades-long search for its final resting place. The experience connects history, technology and discovery in a way that gives curious visitors a new perspective on a story they may think they already know.

Follow the clues, explore technology, and see how Ballard and his team cracked one of history’s greatest mysteries after more than 70 years beneath the sea.

Exhibit Highlights

See real equipment used during the expedition, including cameras, robotics, and Ballard’s gear
Relive the final days of the search and the thrilling moment of discovery
Experience never-before-seen footage captured during the discovery – and learn why the Titanic was left undisturbed
Discover how this mission inspired a new wave of ocean exploration and sparked a global legacy

Step Aboard the Virtual Titanic

Walk the decks of the Titanic like its 1912 with a jaw-droppingly realistic virtual walkthrough, Project 401.

From the top deck, to passenger halls, to crew quarters, all the way down to the engine room, it’s the closest you’ll get to actually being there.

Find the RMS Titanic Challenge Game

Think you can track down the Titanic wreck? Grab your crew (or go at it alone) in this card game adventure. Outfit your ship, budget your supplies, and set sail from Woods Hole, Massachusetts to hunt for the wreck. Every choice matters once you hit the open ocean.

Pilot a Mini ROV

Take the controls of a mini robot sub and steer it through real nautical challenges.

Morse Code Activity

Crack the code! Translate secret messages, then tap out your own in Morse to send to friends.

Parlor Games

Play giant, larger-than-life versions of the games Titanic passengers enjoyed on deck and in the ship’s lounges.

Titanic Pocket Science Demos

Catch Da Vinci Science Center educators live for pop-up science demos, revealing the massive ocean forces Dr. Robert Ballard’s team battled to find and reach the Titanic wreck.

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission is a traveling exhibition produced by Flying Fish in collaboration with Ocean Exploration Trust and generously sponsored by the Office of Naval Research and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

event.title: Otter Chat
event.description:
Otter Chat Daily at 3 p.m.

Meet our playful North American River Otters up-close during an otter chat, and discover more about these fascinating “water weasels” and their care here at the science center. 

Watch our Animal Care team in action as they care for the otters and engage in an interactive chat full of fun facts and behind-the-scenes insights into these amazing creatures.

It’s a must-see experience for animal lovers of all ages!

Otter chats are included with general admission or membership.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

Opening Sept. 29, 2026

Get Tickets

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission invites guests to step into the story behind the 1985 discovery of the RMS Titanic and uncover the classified U.S. Navy mission that helped make it possible.

Visitors can follow the clues that led oceanographer Dr. Robert Ballard and his team to Titanic, learn how deep-sea technology was used to explore more than two miles beneath the North Atlantic, and discover how a secret mission to survey the wrecks of the USS Thresher and USS Scorpion ultimately helped solve one of history’s greatest mysteries.

Along the way, guests will explore the story of Titanic itself, from its launch in 1911 and tragic maiden voyage to the decades-long search for its final resting place. The experience connects history, technology and discovery in a way that gives curious visitors a new perspective on a story they may think they already know.

Follow the clues, explore technology, and see how Ballard and his team cracked one of history’s greatest mysteries after more than 70 years beneath the sea.

Exhibit Highlights

See real equipment used during the expedition, including cameras, robotics, and Ballard’s gear
Relive the final days of the search and the thrilling moment of discovery
Experience never-before-seen footage captured during the discovery – and learn why the Titanic was left undisturbed
Discover how this mission inspired a new wave of ocean exploration and sparked a global legacy

Step Aboard the Virtual Titanic

Walk the decks of the Titanic like its 1912 with a jaw-droppingly realistic virtual walkthrough, Project 401.

From the top deck, to passenger halls, to crew quarters, all the way down to the engine room, it’s the closest you’ll get to actually being there.

Find the RMS Titanic Challenge Game

Think you can track down the Titanic wreck? Grab your crew (or go at it alone) in this card game adventure. Outfit your ship, budget your supplies, and set sail from Woods Hole, Massachusetts to hunt for the wreck. Every choice matters once you hit the open ocean.

Pilot a Mini ROV

Take the controls of a mini robot sub and steer it through real nautical challenges.

Morse Code Activity

Crack the code! Translate secret messages, then tap out your own in Morse to send to friends.

Parlor Games

Play giant, larger-than-life versions of the games Titanic passengers enjoyed on deck and in the ship’s lounges.

Titanic Pocket Science Demos

Catch Da Vinci Science Center educators live for pop-up science demos, revealing the massive ocean forces Dr. Robert Ballard’s team battled to find and reach the Titanic wreck.

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission is a traveling exhibition produced by Flying Fish in collaboration with Ocean Exploration Trust and generously sponsored by the Office of Naval Research and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

event.title: Otter Chat
event.description:

event.title: Women in Science & Engineering Forum
event.description:
The annual Women in Science & Engineering (WISE) Forum brings together high school and college students who are interested in Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts, and Math (STEAM) with accomplished women professionals in STEAM fields, ranging from academia and healthcare to design engineering and space exploration.

A Two-Part Event

The first half of the evening consists of a Distinguished Leader Panel Discussion. We encourage everyone who allies with girls and women in STEAM to attend. The panel features four distinguished women in STEAM who share their perspectives on working in STEAM fields. Hear about the opportunities and challenges they have faced while pursuing careers dominated by men.

Following the panel discussion is a Networking & Mentoring Reception where attendees are invited to connect. This is an opportunity for high school students to talk one-on-one with and receive advice from women professionals and college students.  

Past panelists: executives from DuPont Company; IBM; Mack Trucks; Mars Inc.; Merck; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; and Sanofi. 

Not Just for Women & Girls

Our WISE Initiative and Forum is not just for women and girls. Check out some frequently asked questions below to learn why you should get involved and how to participate.

Is the WISE Forum just for women and girls?

Absolutely not! While the primary goal of the WISE Initiative is to create a supportive community of women employed in STEAM fields and encourage girls who aspire to follow a STEAM career path, all genders can benefit from hearing the stories and experiences shared in the WISE Forum.  

I'm not a woman, why should I care about the WISE Forum?

It’s not only women and girls who need to be informed of the challenges unique to their gender in STEAM careers. Because all genders have a role in creating barriers to an equitable workforce, everyone must learn and improve together to create meaningful change.   

Other communities are also underrepresented in STEAM fields.  While this event is specific to women’s experiences, many discussions and strategies for enacting change also apply to similar challenges faced by other groups, such as people of color and the LGBTQ+ community. 

Many WISE participants also share how other aspects of their identity, in addition to their gender, shape their experiences in the workplace and school. 

What can I take away from this event as a man or someone who does not identify as a woman or girl?

Listening to the personal experiences of panelists, mentors, and students will give you additional perspective on the challenges women and girls encounter. Some stories may be surprising or unexpected and may help you reflect on your personal contribution to an equitable workplace and learning environment. Hearing about these experiences can help you to enact change and become an even better ally and advocate for women in STEAM careers.

This Year’s Panelists

Anne Baum, Founder & Managing Director, Vision Accomplished, LLC (Moderator)

Anne Baum is the Founder and Managing Director of Vision Accomplished, LLC, a consulting firm dedicated to leadership development, executive coaching, and culture development. She is the former President of Lehigh Valley Reilly Children’s Hospital, where she led strategic planning and operations for the first and largest children’s hospital in the Lehigh Valley Region. 

Learn More About Anne

Ayana Ife, Founder & CEO, Ayana Active

Ayana Ife is the Founder and CEO of Ayana Active, a sustainable modest activewear brand designing innovative performance apparel that empowers women through intentional design. With more than 16 years of experience in fashion design and product development, she combines creativity, innovation, and entrepreneurship to create solutions for an underserved market.

Learn More About Ayana

Tammy Klotz, Cybersecurity & IT Executive

Tammy Klotz is a vibrant and accomplished executive and best-selling author with over three decades of diverse experience in the manufacturing industry, specializing in cybersecurity and transformational leadership. She offers keen expertise in navigating mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures within both publicly-traded and privately-held companies and is seasoned in security, risk, and compliance leadership.

Learn More About Tammy

Dr. Karen Peralta Martinez, Bioinformatics Scientist, Nestlé Health Science

Dr. Karen Peralta Martinez is a Bioinformatics Scientist at Nestlé Health Science, where she supports pharmaceutical research and development for VOWST, an FDA-approved microbiome therapeutic. In her role, she applies bioinformatics, multi-omics, and computational biology approaches to advance microbiome research, biomarker discovery, and translational development. 


Learn More About Karen

Dr. Ahna Skop, Professor of Genetics at University of Wisconsin-Madison, Co-Founder & Chief Scientific Officer at aMBR Genomics

Dr. Ahna Skop is an internationally recognized geneticist, cell biologist, artist, and science communicator at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, where she holds joint appointments in Genetics, Cell and Regenerative Biology, Life Sciences Communication, and the Division of the Arts. She is renowned for her pioneering research on the molecular mechanisms of cell division, particularly the discovery and functional characterization of midbody remnants (MBRs) as RNA-rich organelles with emerging roles in cancer and neurodevelopmental disease.

Learn More About Ahna

Visitors can follow the clues that led oceanographer Dr. Robert Ballard and his team to Titanic, learn how deep-sea technology was used to explore more than two miles beneath the North Atlantic, and discover how a secret mission to survey the wrecks of the USS Thresher and USS Scorpion ultimately helped solve one of history’s greatest mysteries.

Along the way, guests will explore the story of Titanic itself, from its launch in 1911 and tragic maiden voyage to the decades-long search for its final resting place. The experience connects history, technology and discovery in a way that gives curious visitors a new perspective on a story they may think they already know.

Follow the clues, explore technology, and see how Ballard and his team cracked one of history’s greatest mysteries after more than 70 years beneath the sea.

Exhibit Highlights

See real equipment used during the expedition, including cameras, robotics, and Ballard’s gear
Relive the final days of the search and the thrilling moment of discovery
Experience never-before-seen footage captured during the discovery – and learn why the Titanic was left undisturbed
Discover how this mission inspired a new wave of ocean exploration and sparked a global legacy

Walk the decks of the Titanic like its 1912 with a jaw-droppingly realistic virtual walkthrough, Project 401.

Pilot a Mini ROV

Take the controls of a mini robot sub and steer it through real nautical challenges.

Morse Code Activity

Crack the code! Translate secret messages, then tap out your own in Morse to send to friends.

Parlor Games

Play giant, larger-than-life versions of the games Titanic passengers enjoyed on deck and in the ship’s lounges.

Catch Da Vinci Science Center educators live for pop-up science demos, revealing the massive ocean forces Dr. Robert Ballard’s team battled to find and reach the Titanic wreck.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission
event.description:
Opening Sept. 29, 2026

Get Tickets

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission invites guests to step into the story behind the 1985 discovery of the RMS Titanic and uncover the classified U.S. Navy mission that helped make it possible.

Visitors can follow the clues that led oceanographer Dr. Robert Ballard and his team to Titanic, learn how deep-sea technology was used to explore more than two miles beneath the North Atlantic, and discover how a secret mission to survey the wrecks of the USS Thresher and USS Scorpion ultimately helped solve one of history’s greatest mysteries.

Along the way, guests will explore the story of Titanic itself, from its launch in 1911 and tragic maiden voyage to the decades-long search for its final resting place. The experience connects history, technology and discovery in a way that gives curious visitors a new perspective on a story they may think they already know.

Follow the clues, explore technology, and see how Ballard and his team cracked one of history’s greatest mysteries after more than 70 years beneath the sea.

Exhibit Highlights

See real equipment used during the expedition, including cameras, robotics, and Ballard’s gear
Relive the final days of the search and the thrilling moment of discovery
Experience never-before-seen footage captured during the discovery – and learn why the Titanic was left undisturbed
Discover how this mission inspired a new wave of ocean exploration and sparked a global legacy

Step Aboard the Virtual Titanic

Walk the decks of the Titanic like its 1912 with a jaw-droppingly realistic virtual walkthrough, Project 401.

From the top deck, to passenger halls, to crew quarters, all the way down to the engine room, it’s the closest you’ll get to actually being there.

Find the RMS Titanic Challenge Game

Think you can track down the Titanic wreck? Grab your crew (or go at it alone) in this card game adventure. Outfit your ship, budget your supplies, and set sail from Woods Hole, Massachusetts to hunt for the wreck. Every choice matters once you hit the open ocean.

Pilot a Mini ROV

Take the controls of a mini robot sub and steer it through real nautical challenges.

Morse Code Activity

Crack the code! Translate secret messages, then tap out your own in Morse to send to friends.

Parlor Games

Play giant, larger-than-life versions of the games Titanic passengers enjoyed on deck and in the ship’s lounges.

Titanic Pocket Science Demos

Catch Da Vinci Science Center educators live for pop-up science demos, revealing the massive ocean forces Dr. Robert Ballard’s team battled to find and reach the Titanic wreck.

Finding Titanic: The Secret Mission is a traveling exhibition produced by Flying Fish in collaboration with Ocean Exploration Trust and generously sponsored by the Office of Naval Research and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Sensory Hour
event.description:
10-11 a.m. on the first Sunday of the month
Beginning Jan. 4

Da Vinci Science Center at PPL Pavilion’s Sensory Hour offers a supportive and welcoming science center experience for guests who benefit from a calmer, sensory-friendly environment. During this dedicated hour, the science center adjusts lighting, sound, and exhibit effects to reduce sensory stimulation while still encouraging exploration and discovery.

What to expect during Sensory Hour:

  • Reduced sound and visual effects throughout the science center
  • A quieter environment at the start of our regular operating hours
  • Sensory support items are always available at the Visitors Services desk, including weighted blankets and noise reducing headsets.
  • We also invite guests to use the Safe Haven room, located near the first floor restrooms, if needed.

Sensory Map

This map notes areas where individuals or caretakers of individuals with several types of sensory sensitivities may want to exercise caution.

Download Sensory Map

Sensory adjustments include:

  • Sound turned down or off on multiple exhibits
  • Sound reduced in the traveling exhibit
  • Touch Lightning exhibit (Tesla Coil) turned off
  • Victaulic Pipe Organ paddles removed
  • Volume lowered in Curiosity Hall
  • Immersive experiences muted
  • Pocono Ravine in Lehigh River Watershed: bird sounds turned off and water features off
  • Limestone Cavern in Lehigh River Watershed: bat sounds turned off and graphic disabled

Sensory Hour is designed for individuals with sensory sensitivities, neurodivergent guests, and anyone who prefers a quieter museum experience. Families, caregivers, and guests of all ages are welcome.

We are also happy to take comments or suggestions at the Visitor Services desk and appreciate any feedback you and your family might share with us!

Social Narrative

A social narrative, or social story, is a learning tool that parents, guardians, caretakers, and teachers can use to help children understand important social parts of an event or activity, including things the child may see, how the child may feel, how others may feel or act during the event or activity, and behavioral expectations.

The use of social narratives can help reduce a child’s anxiety over an unknown or difficult social situation and can promote social and behavioral learning.

event.title: Midnight in the Garden Scout Overnight
event.description:
Girl Scouts Overnight Camp-In

Price: $79/scout, $49/ratio adult, $85/additional adult

Spend the night in the science center, featuring a walk-through model of the Lehigh River watershed, including a cave, waterfall and native flora and fauna! Girls will explore ecosystems, native and invasive species, and learn how to design gardens that work with nature. Girls will also learn the science of preserving foods from the garden!  After we’re done, we’ll sleep on our exhibit floor and enjoy a continental breakfast in the morning. 

Scouts will work towards the following badges: Daisy Eco Learner, Brownie Eco Friend, Junior Flowers, Cadette Trees, Senior Eco Explorer, and Ambassador Eco Advocate.

Pizza dinner, a light snack, a continental breakfast, and a Da Vinci Science Center fun patch are included.
